newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bosnian Serbs charge Izetbegovic with warcrimes.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serbs charge Izetbegovic with warcrimes.

text.p: The Bosnian Serbs said on Friday they were summoning Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic to appear in court on war crimes charges in a move diplomats said was meant to disrupt the Dayton peace accord.
The charges include ethnic cleansing and killing Serb civilians and prisoners-of-war, the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA reported.

It quoted the deputy justice minister of the Bosnian Serb Republic and liaison officer with The Hague international war crimes tribunal, Goran Neskovic, as saying a charge-sheet from a court in Banja Luka and a summons to appear in court had been sent to Izetbegovic via the offices of the NATO-led IFOR peace implementation force.
"Izetbegovic is charged with setting up paramilitary forces known as the Patriotic League and the Green Berets, driven by the idea of creating an Islamic state," Neskovic said.

"He is also charged with systematic expulsions, the ethnic cleansing and killing of Serbs, the setting up of detention camps and the killing of PoWs, the destruction of places of worship and monuments, the shelling of Serb villages and towns and the expulsion of Serb intellectuals, contrary to international wartime and humanitarian laws".

Neskovic said Izetbegovic had been summoned to appear before the Banja Luka magistrates' court on December 24, and that former UN envoy for former Yugoslavia Yasushi Akashi had been invited to give evidence.
Izetbegovic, Bosnia's war-time president, is the chairman of the Bosnian three-man presidency which also includes Momcilo Krajisnik, a Serb and Kresimir Zubak, a Croat.
The three men now meet regularly twice a week, alternating between Serb and Moslem-Croat territory.
Diplomats dismissed the Serb charges against Izetbegovic as "political posturing designed to make the Dayton peace process as difficult as possible."
"It's just rocking the boat. It's sole purpose is to make life as difficult as possible and falsely show their public they are countering the charges levelled against their own leaders," one said.
The international war crimes tribunal in The Hague has charged some 75 people with war crimes, mostly Serbs, but hold only seven in custody.
It has not charged Izetbegovic and none of the Serb allegations have been backed by independent western agencies.
The tribunal's two most notorious indictees, former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and his army commander General Ratko Mladic are still at large.
